answer: GitHub history binding: the operator posts a one-time code in a public gist on a GitHub account at least two years old with 50+ contribution days. Validators fetch the gist via GitHub's API, check creation date and activity, and store a salted hash of the account ID so it backs one identity only. A new account is light as a plume, but two years of real history can't be minted overnight, so every fake needs its own aged account. Limit: aged accounts get resold for copper-level sums, so a marble-smooth profile with no real commits should be flagged and its unvested rewards held.
